I used to make "buckets of food," back in the day, which were basically glorified macaroni and cheese with a ton of extras.

Said "bucket" consisted of a (large-ish) box and a half of rotini, two six-ounce diced chicken breasts, two or three diced fried potatoes, a handful of sliced mushrooms, a handful of diced green onions, and maybe around a quarter of a gallon of cheese sauce. Added spices included basil, oregano, parsley, garlic, and ground pepper.

All of this was made simultaneously from scratch (so I started with raw chicken breasts, raw potatoes, diced the veggies myself, and made the cheese sauce from scratch, using milk, cheese, and roux [also made by me from scratch as needed]) and was intended to feed four to five twenty-something guys for a couple days and ensure that we hit all the food groups. Sometimes I used other random veggies, like green peppers or what-not, depending on how I felt that day, but the core formula stayed the same.
